sūtōrĭus , a, um, adj. id.,
I.of or belonging to a shoemaker or cobbler (class.): atramentum, shoemakers' blacking, Cic. Fam. 9, 21, 3; Plin. 20, 12, 48, § 123; 34, 12, 32, § 123; Cels. 5, 8: fistula, a shoemaker's punch, Plin. 17, 14, 23, § 100: “MERX,” Inscr. Orell. 4168 : “Turpio sutorius,” formerly a shoemaker, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 15 : Atrium Sutorium, Shoemakers' Hall, a place in Rome, Varr. L. L. 6, § 14 Müll.; Calend. Praenest. m. Mart. (ap. Inscr. Orell. II., p. 386); v. atrium fin.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
